clue.text: Television series following motor mechanic

indicators.note: following puts the television series after the word for motor

parts.note: a motor is an engine
ER is the long-running American hospital drama

explanation.surface: A TV programme comes on after a garage worker is introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic who maintains machines can be called an engineer, a synonym in that trade sense.

clue.text: Screens Ghost on 1st of September

parts.note: a shade is a ghost or spirit

indicators.note: 1st of picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A spectre appears on the first day of September and blocks things from view.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades are blinds or screens that block light, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: 'Butt' almost transformed into 'but'

indicators.note: almost means the word for butt loses its final letter

parts.note: the butt of a joke is its object or target

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of the word into are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wordplay game in which one word nearly turns into a shorter one.
explanation.walkthrough: The butt of a joke is its object. 'transformed' turns INTO into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'but' is a demur or protest, as in 'no buts', so it is a synonym for a raised complaint.

clue.text: Draws author returning after military service

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the air force abbreviation

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is a branch of the British armed services

indicators.note: returning means the word for author is read backwards

parts.note: the author of a piece may refer to the writer's own self

explanation.surface: A writer comes home after serving in the forces and sketches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives FLES; the author is a writer's self, though Will Self, the novelist, gives it extra point.
explanation.definitionFit: Draws are lotteries in which tickets are pulled at random, so prize draws and these are synonyms.

clue.text: Senseless and mad, but not ultimately dangerous

indicators.note: but not says a letter is taken away from the word for mad

parts.note: mad means insane

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of dangerous

explanation.surface: Describing someone reckless and crazy, though not in the end a threat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something senseless is silly and pointless, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Pulse's gone astray in musical instruction

parts.note: dal is a pulse such as lentils, and the 's adds S

indicators.note: astray says the letters of gone wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician's heartbeat has gone wrong while following a score direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' is not a heartbeat but the lentil dish DAL; 'astray' makes EGNO from GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dal segno is Italian for 'from the sign', a score direction telling the player to go back.

clue.text: Men broadcast rude filth

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of rude are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A group of men airs offensive smut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns RUDE into DURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordure is dung or excrement, and figuratively anything foul, so filth is a synonym.

clue.text: Bugging Head constantly about Hebrew in school

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation goes inside the word for school

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
Heb is the standard abbreviation for Hebrew

explanation.surface: A head teacher is constantly concerned with Hebrew in a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a school's headteacher, but it belongs to the definition: something that bugs your head all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something that occupies your thoughts obsessively and keeps nagging at you.

clue.text: Area covered retrospectively by Messier Catalogue

indicators.note: retrospectively says the hidden letters are read backwards
covered by says the letters sit concealed inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An astronomical list of nebulae and galaxies looked back at for its coverage of the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Area covered' as the definition, leaving the hiding with no signal; 'covered' is that signal, so the definition is just 'Area'.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land measurement, so it names a specific area.

clue.text: Bird's beginning to fly wearing new leg ring

indicators.note: wearing means the bird remnant is put on inside the rearranged leg
new says the letters of leg are made into a fresh order
the beginning of the bird flies off, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: the bird whose start goes missing

explanation.surface: A young bird ready for its first flight has a fresh leg band fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns LEG into GLE; 'fly' is not the insect but the first letter flying away.
explanation.definitionFit: A girdle is a band or belt that encircles something, so a ring around it.

clue.text: 'Distress' walls of house using fashion's foremost interior design fad

indicators.note: foremost takes the opening letter of fashion's
to distress is to batter something into a new state, so the letters are knocked into a new order
the walls of the word house are its outside letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Battering a house's walls to look aged, following the latest fashion, is an interior design craze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distress' in quotes looks like the decorating technique of ageing furniture, but it is the anagram signal for HE, USING and F.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese system of arranging rooms for harmony became a Western home-decorating craze, so a design fad.

clue.text: Eavesdropper's scanned High Street for one dropping litter?

indicators.note: an eavesdropper hears rather than reads, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: scanned, in the past tense, means read, which is said like the colour

indicators.note: high means intoxicated, so the letters of street stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A snoop has looked over the main shopping street, perhaps for a litterbug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Street' looks like a single place but 'High' rearranges STREET into SETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog of this breed gives birth to a litter of puppies, the question mark marking the playful sense of dropping.

clue.text: Bird wishes you hadn't stripped

indicators.note: stripped means the outer layer, the first and last letters, is taken off

parts.note: to regret something is to wish you had not done it

explanation.surface: Someone says they wish you hadn't taken your clothes off.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, so this wading bird is an example of the category.

clue.text: Butt in, taking Jedi's other half instead to bar

indicators.note: instead says one pair of letters replaces another in the word for butt in

parts.note: to butt in with a remark is to interject
the second half of the word Jedi, the part not starting it

explanation.surface: A Star Wars knight's partner interrupts and is stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: JE, the first half of Jedi, sits in the word for butt in; 'taking' the other half 'instead' swaps it out. Swapping the other way would also work, so crossings decide.
explanation.definitionFit: To interdict is to forbid or prohibit formally, so a synonym of barring.

clue.text: Number One resentful about gradual decline

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
sore means aggrieved or resentful

explanation.surface: A top-ranked person, bitter about a slow slide in status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses NOISORE as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is wearing away bit by bit, a slow deterioration.

clue.text: Watch cuckoo line nest

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on a cuckoo as it lines its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: The cuckoo is famous for using other birds' nests, but here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a guard keeping watch, so the noun watch, a lookout, is a synonym.

clue.text: Well aware of popular feeling

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
touch is the sense of feeling

explanation.surface: Someone who knows well what the public is feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means keeping up with and informed about something.

clue.text: Exclusive cash asset's first to become liquid mostly

indicators.note: to become says one letter of cash turns into the shortened liquid
first picks the opening letter of asset's
mostly means the word liquid loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A financier's money is so private that the main holding gets turned largely into cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of CASH, asset's first letter, becomes LIQUI.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliquish group shuts out outsiders, so it is exclusive in the social sense.

clue.text: You can't mean that bully has taken warning to heart

indicators.note: has taken says the bully swallows another word
to heart puts the warning right in the middle of the bully

parts.note: to cow someone is to bully or intimidate them
an omen is a warning sign

explanation.surface: Protesting at a bully who has been unmoved by a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of mild disbelief or reproach, said when someone overstates.

clue.text: It may help you go and manage to fit in exercise

indicators.note: to fit in says the word for manage is placed inside the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Advice on squeezing a workout into a busy day to keep you going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' here means go to the toilet: this dried fruit is a traditional laxative.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried plums are a well-known natural laxative, easing a trip to the lavatory.

clue.text: Knave or jack changing hands

indicators.note: changing says the two letters trade places, completing the swap
hands are left and right, so the letters standing for each are the ones involved

parts.note: jack is a sailor, and a lascar is an East Indian sailor

explanation.surface: A card-game question: is a knave the same as a jack passed between players?
explanation.walkthrough: In cards knave and jack are the same, the obvious false path; here jack is a sailor whose L (left) and R (right) trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest rogue, so the word for a scamp or scoundrel is a synonym.

clue.text: Projection for family that's viewed as 1 in 17

indicators.note: in says the numeral goes inside the pair of synonyms

parts.note: the answer to 17 means at home and touching, read here as synonyms: home for its first word and move, in the sense of stir emotionally, for its second
1 is written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A film for the family, considered as one entry within another.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to the answer of 17, not its clue: its two words are swapped for synonyms, then I goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur footage shot of and for a household is projected for relatives to watch.

clue.text: Aim to profit at the outset, changing the best possible outcomes

indicators.note: changing says the gathered letters are rearranged
at the outset picks the opening letter of profit

explanation.surface: A business strategy: go for profit from the start and alter course for top results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges AIMTO plus P.
explanation.definitionFit: Optima is the Latin plural of optimum, the most favourable result.

clue.text: Hoisted American flag in tree

indicators.note: hoisted means raised up, which in a down entry reads the pieces from the bottom up

parts.note: a flag, or flagstone, is a paving slab

explanation.surface: The Stars and Stripes has been run up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is a paving stone; 'Hoisted' reverses ASLAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a tropical American tree known for its very light wood.

clue.text: Sound of hissing initially when Serpent's cross

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, and the setter calls himself Serpent; the 's stands for is
cross means angry, irate

explanation.surface: The setter's snake hisses when annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Serpent is the setter's own pseudonym. 'Sound of hissing initially' is the h-sound at the start of hissing.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics an aspirate is the breathy h sound, which opens that word.

clue.text: The result when one's routed a different way

definitions.text: The result when one's routed a different way

indicators.note: a different way says the letters of routed are put in another order

explanation.surface: What happens when a traveller is sent along another road.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion from the usual route is what you face when sent another way round.

clue.text: Flag leads to violent exchanges at the end of every year

indicators.note: at the end of puts the first letters after the yearly abbreviation

parts.note: PA, per annum, means every year

indicators.note: leads to takes the opening letters of violent and exchanges

explanation.surface: A warning sign that annual rows turn into fights.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag a path is to lay flagstones on it, which is to surface it with paving.

clue.text: Wet weather conditions block two roads

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to block it
MI is the M1 motorway, Britain's main north-south road, and St is street

explanation.surface: Rain and fog close two roads.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch mist is a thick drizzling fog, common in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a mixture of fine drizzle and mist, a sort of damp weather.
